note: Phase definitions of the strategy PDF, extracted verbatim (no timelines by decision). The PDF is built from the same text.

phases.name: Foundations
phases.goal: Everything every NF needs, plus the legal and process groundwork, so the five NFs are built on one consistent base.
deliverables: Repo scaffold, toolchain pin, CI pipeline, lint/format, container builds, licence scan + SBOM.
ADRs D1–D5 decided and recorded; spec baseline (Rel-16 TS list and versions) in docs/specs; clause-to-module traceability table.
libs/sbi: HTTP/2 server/client, JSON (de)serialisation, OpenAPI-driven model generation from 3GPP YAML, ProblemDetails, retry/timeouts, TLS, OAuth2 token hooks.
libs/nas (TS 24.501 5GMM/5GSM), libs/ngap (TS 38.413, own ASN.1 pipeline), libs/pfcp (TS 29.244), libs/gtpu (TS 29.281).
libs/crypto: Milenage, 5G-AKA / 5G key hierarchy (KAUSF→KSEAF→KAMF→KgNB), SUCI ECIES profiles A and B, NEA0-3 / NIA0-3.
libs/config, telemetry, testkit: YAML config with validation, logging/metrics/tracing, packet builders, mock-peer harness.
Compose environment bringing up UERANSIM and Open5GS (as oracle) so baseline traces exist from day one; capture golden pcaps of S1–S3 from Open5GS.
validation: Codec round-trip tests on captured Open5GS/UERANSIM pcaps; decoders fuzzed for a fixed time budget.
Crypto matches published vectors in TS 35.208 and TS 33.501 annexes.
exit: CI green on all libs; licence scan clean; fuzzing running.
risks: ASN.1 toolchain choice can be a time sink – time-box and decide early.
Scope creep into “perfect” libs: implement Rel-16 SA subset needed for S1–S8 only.

phases.name: UDM (+ UDR-lite, AUSF-lite)
phases.goal: A working subscriber-data and authentication backbone, exercised by mock consumers, before any RAN exists.
deliverables: UDM services: Nudm_UEAuthentication (generate auth data, auth-event confirm), Nudm_SubscriberDataManagement (AM, SM, NSSAI data; subscribe/notify), Nudm_UEContextManagement (AMF/SMF registration).
SUCI de-concealment (home network private key handling, profiles A/B) and SUPI resolution.
Subscriber provisioning: REST + CLI for IMSI, K/OPc, AMF field, SQN, DNN/slice profile. Secure storage of K/OPc (envelope encryption hook for later HSM/KMS).
SQN management and resynchronisation (AUTS handling).
shims/udr-lite (Nudr_DataRepository subset) and shims/ausf-lite (Nausf_UEAuthentication 5G-AKA subset) strictly as needed.
validation: Auth vectors compared with Open5GS UDM output for identical K/OPc/RAND/SQN.
Mock AMF/AUSF clients drive all UDM operations; negative tests (unknown SUPI, bad SUCI scheme, SQN mismatch).
exit: Bit-exact vectors match the oracle and spec.
Provisioning round-trip works; 1,000 auth req/s on one core-class instance (baseline).
risks: Key handling is security-critical: code review + threat note before exit.
Keep shims minimal or they become legacy we must migrate.

phases.name: PCF
phases.goal: Policy decisions available to SMF and AMF with subscriber-linked policy data.
deliverables: Npcf_SMPolicyControl (create/update/delete; PCC rules, QoS (5QI, ARP, AMBR), session rules) and Npcf_AMPolicyControl.
Policy store via UDR-lite; default policy profile plus per-subscriber / per-DNN overrides; policy templates in config.
Policy-update notifications toward SMF (Npcf_SMPolicyControl_UpdateNotify).
Hooks reserved (not built) for UE policy (UCU), AF-influenced traffic (N5) and usage monitoring – Phase 7/8.
specs: TS 23.503; TS 29.512 (SM policy); TS 29.507 (AM policy); TS 29.519 (policy data in UDR).
validation: Component tests with mock SMF/AMF; policy decision tables tested against spec examples.
Interop: Open5GS SMF ↔ our PCF, with identical QoS outcome in the SMF trace.
exit: Open5GS SMF accepts our PCF decisions for S2-style sessions.
Policy change mid-session reaches the SMF.
risks: Behavioural differences in optional IEs between implementations – capture in update.md as they surface.

phases.name: UPF
phases.goal: A correct, then fast, user plane that any spec-compliant SMF can drive.
deliverables: PFCP (N4): association setup/heartbeat/release, session establishment/modification/deletion/report; PDR, FAR, QER, URR, BAR; UE IP pool hooks; SDF filter matching.
GTP-U (N3/N9): encapsulation/decapsulation, echo, error indication, end-marker, extension headers (PDU Session Container, QFI).
N6: TUN/TAP and routed interface to the data network; NAT/masquerade as config option.
QoS enforcement: session-AMBR, MBR/GBR per QER, QFI marking. Usage reports (volume/time) for future charging.
Stage A: userspace datapath for correctness. Stage B: AF_XDP/eBPF fast path; multi-queue, RSS, CPU pinning. Benchmarks published in docs.
validation: Driven by a scripted PFCP client and (interop) Open5GS SMF ↔ our UPF with UERANSIM traffic.
Packet-level tests: golden GTP-U frames in/out; fuzzing of PFCP and GTP-U parsers.
iperf3/TRex throughput and latency at increasing UE/session counts.
exit: Open5GS SMF + UERANSIM: ping and iperf through our UPF.
Stage A: ≥ 1 Gbps single host; target for Stage B set as an ADR (e.g. 10 Gbps).
risks: Performance work can swallow effort – gate it behind correctness.
Windows is a dev host only; UPF development and performance testing need Linux (WSL2/VM).

phases.name: SMF
phases.goal: Complete PDU session lifecycle control across UDM, PCF, UPF and (mock) AMF.
deliverables: Nsmf_PDUSession: Create/Update/Release SM Context (from AMF), N1N2 message transfer, status notify.
5GSM NAS handling via AMF (establishment accept/reject, modification, release) using libs/nas.
N4 control: UPF association management, UPF selection (DNN, slice, load/static), rule generation from PCC rules (PDR/FAR/QER).
IP address management (IPv4, IPv6 prefix, IPv4v6), DNN/DNS/MTU config, session AMBR, QoS flow mapping (default + dedicated).
UDM subscription retrieval (SM data) and PCF SM policy integration; session/SM-context persistence to external store.
Handling of UPF failure/restart, N4 session recovery; idempotent retries.
specs: TS 23.502 §4.3 (PDU session procedures); TS 29.502; TS 24.501 (5GSM); TS 29.244.
validation: Mock AMF drives full lifecycle; real UPF (ours) + real PCF/UDM (ours).
Interop: Open5GS AMF ↔ our SMF ↔ Open5GS UPF and our UPF (all combinations) with UERANSIM.
exit: S2, S3, S5 (partial) pass with Open5GS AMF in front; pcap diff on N4 shows no semantic deviations.
Crash/restart test: sessions recovered or cleanly released.
risks: QoS/PCC-to-PFCP mapping is the most intricate logic – build a rule-mapping test table from spec early.

phases.name: AMF
phases.goal: The last and most complex of the five: real UE and gNB attach to our core end to end.
deliverables: N2/NGAP: SCTP endpoint, NG Setup, gNB/UE context, Initial UE Message, UL/DL NAS transport, Initial Context Setup, UE Context Release, PDU Session Resource Setup/Modify/Release, Paging, Reset, Error Indication.

NAS (5GMM): Registration (initial/mobility/periodic), Authentication, Security Mode (integrity + ciphering), Identity, Configuration Update, Service Request, Deregistration, Notification; GUTI allocation; 5G-TMSI paging.
UE context and registration-area management, tracking-area lists, allowed NSSAI from config/UDM, 5GMM timers.
SBI: Namf_Communication, Namf_EventExposure (basic), calls to AUSF (shim), UDM, PCF (AM policy), SMF.
Handover: Xn-based path switch, then N2-based handover (S6). Multi-gNB support.
Stateless-ready design: UE context externalised for later HA; SCTP multi-homing config.
specs: TS 23.502 §4.2 (registration, service request, deregistration), §4.9 (handover); TS 24.501; TS 38.413; TS 29.518; TS 33.501 §6 (security procedures).
validation: Replay of captured Open5GS/UERANSIM NAS/NGAP traces as decoder and state-machine tests.
UERANSIM gNB + UE: S1, S2, S3, S4; then srsRAN and the ORAN emulator.
exit: Phase-5 milestone: UERANSIM UE registers, establishes a PDU session and pings 8.8.8.8 through our 5 NFs (plus shims).
S1–S4 green on UERANSIM and on the ORAN emulator.
risks: NAS/NGAP edge cases and timer behaviour are where interop bugs hide – use traces and fuzzing heavily.
Security-mode/ciphering errors look like generic failures – invest in good diagnostics early.

phases.name: Integration & validation of the 5-NF core
phases.goal: Prove the five-NF core works as a system, independently of any single-phase test, and establish the regression suite we keep forever.
deliverables: Full S1–S8 on UERANSIM, srsRAN (ZMQ) and the ORAN emulator; multi-UE, multi-session scale tests (100 → 1,000 → 10,000 simulated UEs).
Conformance matrix: each procedure → clause → test → status, published in docs/specs; differential pcap analysis against Open5GS.
72-hour soak, memory-leak and FD-leak checks, failure injection (kill NF, drop N4/N11, SCTP flaps).
Bug-burn-down and performance baseline report; decision checkpoint before Phases 7–9.
specs: Whole-system view of TS 23.502 procedures in scope.
exit: ≥ 95% of in-scope scenarios pass on all three RAN peers; no P1 bugs open; soak clean.
risks: Differences between RAN simulators’ behaviours – treat the spec as the tiebreaker, record rulings in ADRs.

phases.name: Remaining NFs and shim removal
phases.goal: Complete the 11-NF core and retire all temporary code.
deliverables: NRF (Nnrf_NFManagement, NFDiscovery, AccessToken; heartbeat/status notify) – first, since every NF then switches from static config to discovery.
AUSF and UDR replace the shims (full 5G-AKA, EAP-AKA’ optional; full Nudr data sets, PostgreSQL-backed).
NSSF (slice selection, NSSAI availability), NEF (northbound exposure, AF traffic influence, monitoring events, CAPIF-ready hooks).
11th NF: SCP for indirect communication and routing (built, ADR-0023); BSF for PCF binding built as an optional twelfth (ADR-0024).
PCF extensions: UE policy, N5/AF interaction, usage monitoring. Optional: UDM/AMF event exposure completion.
validation: Regression: the full Phase-6 suite must still pass, unchanged, after each shim is replaced.
exit: All 11 NFs deployed; shims/ deleted; multi-slice scenarios (S8) green.
risks: Regressions while swapping shims – keep the same external APIs and run the Phase-6 suite on every PR.

phases.name: Production hardening
phases.goal: Turn a working core into an operable, secure, scalable product.
deliverables: HA and scale: stateless NF replicas, external session/UE stores (PostgreSQL / Redis-class), SCTP and N4 failover, rolling upgrades, horizontal autoscaling.

Security: mTLS between all NFs, OAuth2 with NRF tokens enforced, secrets management (KMS/HSM for K/OPc and home-network keys), threat model, pen-test, dependency and container scanning, SBOM and signed artifacts.
Operations: Helm charts/operators, config hot-reload, health probes, Prometheus + Grafana dashboards, alert rules, structured audit logs, runbooks.
Performance: UPF tuning (10–100 Gbps targets by ADR), control-plane registrations/sec and sessions/sec targets, latency SLOs.
Operator features: charging hooks/CDR export (Nchf integration point), lawful-intercept interface design (jurisdiction-dependent), subscriber provisioning API and UI/CLI, multi-PLMN.
Commercial testers: run the conformance scenarios with a commercial core-test tool (Keysight/Spirent class) or a partner lab.
validation: Chaos/failure suite, 7-day soak, load tests to target, external pen-test with remediation.
exit: SLOs and capacity targets met and documented; no critical/high security findings open; upgrade and rollback tested.
risks: Lawful intercept and charging requirements depend on target markets – scope them with stakeholders early.

phases.name: Productisation and release
phases.goal: Package, document, license-audit and ship a release candidate.
deliverables: Versioning and release process, packaged containers/Helm, installation and upgrade guides, operator/admin documentation, API reference.
Final third-party licence audit (automated + manual), NOTICE file, SBOM, patent/FRAND review outcome recorded.
Support tooling: diagnostics bundle, pcap capture, log redaction.
Pilot / field trial plan with a lab or partner network; feedback loop into the backlog.
exit: GA-candidate tagged; licence audit signed off by counsel; pilot plan agreed.
risks: Late discovery of licence or patent issues – mitigated by running checks from Phase 0.
